speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for describing the intense itching and red bumps on your thigh and elsewhere. To better understand what you're dealing with, have you noticed if the bumps appear in clusters or lines, and does the itching worsen at night? Additionally, have you had any recent travel to tropical areas or exposure to insects?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with intense itching of his right thigh region for the past few days. He also mentions the recent formation of ‘red bumps’ in the same area. The patient has recently attended a business conference in Miami. He has a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes type 2, and hyperlipidemia. The patient’s medication regimen includes enalapril, metformin, and atorvastatin. He denies any history of smoking or drinking.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Scabies (infestation by Sarcoptes scabiei). The intense nocturnal itching, linear or clustered "red bumps," and recent close contact at a conference in Miami are classic presentations. Please confirm if you have seen burrow-like tracks or if family members are experiencing similar symptoms.
